figures.title: Three Ways to Connect a Terminal Outcome to Earlier Turns
figures.caption: **Three Ways to Connect a Terminal Outcome to Earlier Turns**: The same trajectory runs a debugger, makes a faulty edit, and fails the terminal check. (a) With only the terminal check, every remaining return equals the one outcome, so the check alone does not separate the useful turn from the faulty one. (b) Learned step scores supply intermediate feedback by adding a criterion to the objective, one the policy can learn to satisfy without progress on the task. (c) Continuation sampling restores each fork condition and averages the returns of its continuations; the difference between the two means estimates how much the debugger turn raised the chance of passing the declared check, with sampling error and without establishing cause.

In panel b, a separate learned scorer box feeds a step score chip under each action along the same kind of rail. In panel c, twenty continuations fan out from h0 and from h1, each ending in a dot that is filled green for a pass and hollow for a fail: 1 of 20 pass from h0 and 12 of 20 pass from h1, labeled K equals 20 per fork. Boxes below read V hat of h0 equals 0.05 and V hat of h1 equals 0.60, and both feed a box reading estimated difference 0.55, standard error at most 0.11 per estimate.

figures.title: Group Barriers and Version-Checked Admission
figures.caption: **Group Barriers and Version-Checked Admission**: (a) In the hypothetical group of four, the barrier holds every slot until the `{python} Straggler.barrier_str` member finishes, leaving `{python} Straggler.idle_str` of reserved slot time idle. (b) Asynchronous collection releases slots early, so the trainer's version advances while rollouts run. Each record carries the version that sampled it, and its lag $\FiniteChange\text{ver}$ at admission grows with its duration; the long rollout exceeds the illustrative bound and is excluded with its reason recorded. (c) A record leaves verification with a pass, a fail, or an unavailable verdict, waits in a bounded group buffer, and reaches the trainer only if its lag is within the bound. While this admission check enforces a strict bound on version lag, it cannot prevent distribution drift when individual gradient updates make large steps in parameter space.
figures.alt: Three stacked panels. Panel a is a to-scale timeline of four rollouts lasting 0.2, 2.1, 4.2, and 16.8 seconds, with hatched idle regions after the first three up to a red dashed barrier, and a trainer row that waits until the barrier before an update; a note reads 65 percent of reserved slot time idle. Panel b shows trainer versions ver through ver plus 4 as consecutive columns above three rollout bars, with a dark tick on each bar wherever it crosses a version boundary, so the number of ticks equals the lag. Rollout A, from ver, crosses one boundary and is admitted at lag 1; rollout B, from ver plus 1, crosses two and is admitted at lag 2; rollout C, from ver, crosses four, ends in a red mark, and is excluded at lag 4; in the lag column a red dashed line labeled delta ver max separates the two admitted lags from the excluded one. Panel c is a flow from a rollout pool sampled at ver b, to verification with pass, fail, or unavailable, to a group buffer drawn as six slots with four filled, to a decision diamond testing whether delta ver is at most delta ver max; the yes branch reaches the trainer, which advances ver t to ver t plus 1, and the no branch leads to a box reading excluded, reason and cost recorded. A return path carries new weights at ver t back to the rollout pool.

figures.title: Restart Policies in a Supervision Tree
figures.caption: **Restart Policies in a Supervision Tree**: Under the one-for-one policy (a), only the failed worker restarts, as a newly admitted attempt with its own reservation, while its siblings continue. Under the one-for-all policy (b), the supervisor stops the coupled siblings through the cancellation protocol and restarts the whole group from recorded inputs, because the caller's partial work has lost its meaning. Either supervisor that exceeds its declared restart intensity stops restarting and escalates the failure to its parent.

Card a, one_for_one: a supervisor with three worker children; the middle worker is marked failed and is the only node inside a dashed red blast radius, with an arrow labeled restart to a new attempt box with its own reservation, while the other two workers are marked continues. Card b, one_for_all: a supervisor with interface, caller, and test children all inside one dashed red blast radius; caller is marked failed, interface and test are marked stopped, and arrows from all three lead to one box labeled group restarts, new attempts from recorded inputs. A dashed red arrow from supervisor b to the parent is labeled restart intensity exceeded, escalate.

figures.caption: **Private Workspaces and Guarded Publication**: Linked worktrees (a) give each worker its own files, index, and HEAD while sharing repository storage; the sandbox around each one, not the worktree, scopes its writes. figures.title: Majority Review Under an Assumed Error Mixture
figures.caption: **Majority Review Under an Assumed Error Mixture**: Every reviewer has the same false-approval rate, $\MarginalFalseApprovalProbability=0.20$. With independent errors (a), majority false approval at five reviewers (open markers) is `{python} ReviewCorrelation.independent_majority_str` and keeps falling as reviewers are added. Under the beta mixture with $\CorrelationCoefficient=0.40$ it is `{python} ReviewCorrelation.mixture_majority_str` and levels off toward the floor $\Pr(\FalseApprovalPropensity>1/2)$ of `{python} ReviewFloor.floor_str`. At five reviewers (b), the mixture shifts probability toward the extremes, so a candidate is either approved by no one or approved by a majority far more often than independence predicts. The curves follow from an assumed beta mixture, not a measured law of model ensembles.
figures.alt: Two panels. Panel a: line chart of majority false approval, 0 to 25 percent, against odd reviewer counts 1 to 15. The solid gray independent-errors line falls from 20 percent toward zero; the dashed red beta-mixture line, rho 0.40, falls only slightly and flattens just above a dotted red floor line near 15 percent labeled Pr of Q greater than one half. The five-reviewer points are open markers. Panel b: grouped bars for 0 to 5 reviewers approving an invalid candidate among five, solid gray for independent errors and red hatched for the beta mixture, with the region for 3 or more shaded as majority approves. The mixture's bar at 0 is the tallest, near 57 percent, and its bars at 3, 4, and 5 exceed the independent ones.

A small purple checkpoint mark sits on each of the four loop arrows. An arrow labeled settled outcome leads from the container down to a slate Acceptance box, Part IV, reading scoped evidence, not the agent's report. A dashed line labeled checked against runs from the task contract around the right side to the acceptance box. actual_steps.title: Delay is distance
actual_steps.description: The brown term is v τ_delay: the plant keeps moving before braking begins. Reducing latency contracts this term without making the braking term disappear.

actual_steps.title: Braking grows faster with speed

figures.title: Three machine classes
figures.caption: **Three machine classes**: Each class is named for the constraint that dominates it and the margin it spends: (a) mass-dominated mobility (Class 1) spends stopping clearance, set by momentum and braking; (b) contact-dominated manipulation (Class 2) spends force and deformation margin, set by contact stiffness and the strength of the object and mechanism; and (c) energy- and thermal-dominated operation (Class 3) spends heat and supply margin, set by Joule heating, thermal capacitance, and power delivery.
figures.alt: Three panels. Class 1, mass-dominated mobility: a wheeled base moving at speed v toward a rack end, with the clear distance D clear marked in red, above the relation d stop equals v tau delay plus v squared over 2 a brake. Class 2, contact-dominated manipulation: an arm whose gripper presses a spring of stiffness k contact into a stiff fixture, deformation delta x and force F in red, above F approximately equals k contact delta x. Class 3, energy- and thermal-dominated: power P in entering a winding of thermal capacitance C th, heat P out leaving, and a temperature bar T wind below a red T limit line, above d T wind over d t equals P in minus P out over C th. Each panel names the margin it spends: stopping clearance, force and deformation margin, heat and supply margin.

figures.title: Three ceilings on the braking base
figures.caption: **Three ceilings on the braking base**: (a) Only the driven wheels brake against the floor, so friction there caps the retarding force at $\CoulombFrictionCoefficient \DrivenWheelLoadFraction \Mass \Gravity$; the credible `{python} BrakingLimits.a_req_str` needs $\CoulombFrictionCoefficient \ge$ `{python} BrakingLimits.mu_min_str` with all the weight on those wheels and `{python} BrakingLimits.mu_min_rated_str` at their rated load share. The inertial load $\Mass \CredibleBrakingDeceleration$ acts at the center of gravity, a height $\GravityCenterHeight$ above the floor, and pitches the body about its leading support unless $\GravityCenterHeight/\LeadingSupportDistance \le$ `{python} BrakingLimits.cg_ratio_max_str`; neither length has been measured. (b) Each direct-drive hub wheel turns its `{python} BrakingLimits.tau_wheel_str` current-limited torque into a floor force $\DriveBrakingTorqueCeiling/\WheelRadius$, `{python} BrakingLimits.force_str` for the pair, and the spinning parts are already counted in $\EffectiveImpactMass$. The layout is schematic, not to scale.
figures.alt: Two panels. Panel a: side view of a mobile base with a tote rack and an arm, a driven wheel between two casters, and a center of gravity marker. Arrows show the weight m g downward and the inertial load m a brake forward at the center of gravity, normal loads phi m g on the driven wheel and on the casters, and a friction force F at most mu phi m g at the driven wheel pointing against travel. Dimension lines mark the unmeasured height h cg and the distance d lead to the front caster. A red curved arrow at the front caster reads tips if h cg over d lead exceeds 4.90. A line below reads mu at least 0.204 at phi equals 1 and at least 0.250 at the rated phi of 0.815. Panel b: one hub wheel with a hub motor of ratio 1, a braking torque tau equals 60 newton meters, radius 133 millimeters, and a floor force of 451 newtons; notes read two wheels 902 newtons, m eff at most 387 kilograms, and a ceiling of at least 2.33 meters per second squared.

figures.title: Strain wave gear set
figures.caption: **Strain wave gear set**: The three parts of a Harmonic Drive strain wave gear, disassembled: the elliptical wave generator with its thin-race ball bearing (top left), the flexspline cup with external teeth on its open rim (top right), and the rigid circular spline ring with internal teeth (bottom). The wave generator bends the flexspline so that its teeth mesh with the circular spline at two opposite zones; because the flexspline carries slightly fewer teeth, each turn of the wave generator advances it by only that difference, which gives a high reduction with little backlash. figures.caption: **Torque, speed, and time on one joint motor**: (a) The TQ-RoboDrive ILM 70x18 of the arm's stand-in joint on its `{python} TorqueSpeedEnvelope.v_bus_str` supply. figures.title: Two-speed brain architecture
figures.caption: **Two-speed brain architecture**: Above the proposal boundary, two learned proposers run at their own rates, an intent model at `{python} TwoSpeedRates.f_intent_str` and a chunk policy renewing at `{python} TwoSpeedRates.f_chunk_str`. Below it, the permission path checks each proposal against measured state on a `{python} TwoSpeedRates.f_tick_str` tick, and the drives close their own current and velocity loops. A proposal carries no authority until it is admitted; a refusal returns the proposers to a plan from measured state.
figures.alt: Two regions separated by a dashed vertical line labeled proposal boundary. Left region, Brain learned proposers: observations feed an intent model at 2 hertz and 336 milliseconds per evaluation, which passes a goal to a chunk policy at 20 hertz renewal and 40 milliseconds inference; a state resynchronization box below feeds the chunk policy. Right region, Nervous System and Body: encoders and scanner feed a permission path at a 1 kilohertz tick, which sends an admitted command to drives with current and velocity loops, which move the physical plant; the plant feeds back to the encoders. A dashed proposal arrow crosses from the chunk policy to the permission path, and a dashed refusal arrow returns from the permission path to state resynchronization.

figures.title: Embodied Vision-Language-Action (VLA) architecture
figures.caption: **Embodied Vision-Language-Action (VLA) architecture**: A representative dataflow. (1) Camera patches receive 2D image-position and camera identifiers alongside language and robot-state tokens; metric depth still requires calibrated evidence. (2) Self-attention mixes the combined token sequence; the colored grid illustrates internal attention weights, not a verified affordance or grasp pose. (3) Autoregressive token decoders emit tokens sequentially, whereas one-pass chunk heads and iterative action experts generate candidate multi-step chunks ($\PolicyActionWindow$) in one pass or over several refinement steps. (4) An independent permission path checks candidate motion against sensed state and modeled limits before actuation. (Synthesized from Brohan et al. [@brohan2023rt1; @brohan2023rt2], Kim et al. [@kim2024openvla], and Octo Model Team [@octo_2023]).

figures.title: Topological vision-language navigation
figures.caption: **Topological vision-language navigation**: Embodied navigation architecture executing natural-language spatial instructions. figures.title: The physical AI cognitive flow
figures.caption: **The physical AI cognitive flow**: The learned stages run on the application processor and each hands the next a record that ages: ingestion produces tokens, perception a metric pose with its age, memory a belief with its evidence epoch, intent an intent lease, and planning candidate setpoints. Everything up to planning is proposal. Only the permission path, on its own `{python} TwoSpeedRates.f_tick_str` tick across the proposal boundary, can turn a proposal into an admitted command for the drives.

An arrow wraps from memory down to the second row: intent (hands on intent lease) feeds planning (hands on candidate setpoints). The learned stages sit inside a dashed region labeled application processor. A dashed proposal arrow from planning crosses a vertical dashed line labeled proposal boundary into a permission path box (safety MCU, 1 kHz tick), which sends an admitted command to drives and plant.

figures.title: Illustrative embodied roofline
figures.caption: **Illustrative embodied roofline**: Arithmetic intensity (operations per byte moved from off-chip memory, @eq-brain-arithmetic-intensity) against attainable throughput using the application processor's dense FP16 GPU ceiling and rounded peak memory bandwidth. Single-token weight streaming sits deep in the memory-bound region, while the intent model's prefill, which reuses each fetched weight across all of its input tokens, lies past the ridge, the intensity at which the bandwidth roof meets the compute roof, where compute binds. Chunk length alone does not determine arithmetic intensity; chunked workloads require measured operations and memory traffic. A separate real-time loop executes accepted waypoints between fresh model updates.

figures.caption: **Chunk supply against the evidence horizon**: With direct replacement, time runs from the capture that the first chunk is computed from. The chunk policy renews every `{python} ConveyorChunkSizing.chunk_period_str` and needs `{python} ConveyorChunkSizing.chunk_latency_str` per evaluation, so each chunk is in force for one renewal period and is replaced when its evidence is `{python} ConveyorChunkSizing.open_loop_str` old. figures.title: The two-processor implementation
figures.caption: **The two-processor implementation**: The application processor runs the learned proposers and has no access to the drive registers. Proposals cross a black-channel board link as framed packets into a double buffer in the microcontroller's own memory. The receive DMA fills a private receive buffer, and the receive interrupt copies each checked frame into the seqlock-guarded mailbox slot, so the processors share no memory. The permission tick reads the latest proposal, checks it against measured state, freshness, and the lease, and sends only an admitted command to the drives, which close their own current and velocity loops. Measured state returns to the application processor as telemetry over the same link.
figures.alt: Three horizontal tiers. Top, application processor: perception feeds an intent model at 2 hertz, which passes a goal to a chunk policy at 20 hertz renewal. Middle band: a dashed black-channel board link, a serial peripheral interface (SPI) bus or a Controller Area Network with Flexible Data-Rate (CAN FD) bus, framed packets with CRC and sequence number, no shared memory. A dashed proposal arrow runs from the chunk policy through the link into a double buffer with seqlock, filled by receive DMA in MCU-local SRAM, inside the safety MCU. The buffer feeds a permission tick at 1 kilohertz that checks freshness, lease, and limits. Bottom: the tick sends an admitted command to drives with current and velocity loops, which move the physical plant; the plant feeds back to encoders and scanner, which feed the permission tick and send telemetry up through the link to perception.
figures.systems_goal: Follow a checked proposal across processors without implying shared memory.

figures.title: Multi-rate cadence and the mailbox exchange
figures.caption: **Multi-rate cadence and the mailbox exchange**: (a) The running machine's clocks during a proposer stall, to scale. The chunk policy renews every `{python} MultirateStall.t_renew_str` and needs `{python} MultirateStall.t_infer_str`; the admitted chunk supplies a setpoint every `{python} MultirateStall.t_step_str`. When the third renewal never completes, the tick keeps executing the admitted chunk only until the `{python} MultirateStall.t_lease_str` lease from the last admission lapses; the tick, bus, and brake onset then put the fallback stop `{python} MultirateStall.renewal_to_onset_str` after that admission. (b) The single-slot seqlock in the microcontroller's own memory, in event order. The receive interrupt makes the counter odd, copies a checked frame, and makes it even; the tick accepts a copy only when it reads the same even value before and after. A tick that preempts a write reads an odd value and keeps its last validated chunk, and a stalled application processor leaves the slot unchanged while the lease runs.
figures.alt: Two panels. Panel a, a timeline from 0 to about 210 milliseconds with five lanes. Chunk policy: inference bars from 0 to 40 and 50 to 90, then a hatched stalled bar from 100 onward. Setpoints: ticks every 25 milliseconds from 40 to 140. Lease: a dashed outline from 40 to 100 and a filled bar from 90 to 150 labeled lease 60 ms from last admission. Permission tick: fine lines every 1 millisecond. Drives: tracking until 150, a short green interval to 172 labeled tick plus bus plus onset 22 ms, then a red fallback stop. Dashed vertical lines mark last admission at 90, lease expiry at 150, and a red brake onset at 172. Panel b, three lanes in event order: receive ISR writer, sequence counter, and permission tick reader, in three cases. Clean exchange: the writer copies a frame while the counter goes 7 then 8, and the reader reads 8 twice and accepts. Tick preempts a write: the counter reads 9 during a paused write, the reader rejects, then after the counter becomes 10 the reader accepts. Application processor stalls: no frame arrives and the reader reads 10 again twice.
figures.systems_goal: Show how seqlock consistency and lease expiry handle different faults.

figures.title: Hardware proposal boundary
figures.caption: **Hardware proposal boundary**: (a) The application processor proposes across a black-channel board link into the safety microcontroller's own double buffer; the permission path on that microcontroller is the sole writer of the drive registers and can trip a drive inhibit. (b) When the application processor can write the drive registers directly, an unchecked write reaches the motors, and proposer and drives share a single failure domain.
figures.alt: Two panels. (a) Separate permission path: a dashed bronze application processor box, learned proposers with no drive access, sends proposal p t through a dashed black-channel board link with CRC and sequence into a safety MCU container, which has its own memory and is the sole writer of drive registers. Inside it, an MCU-local double buffer feeds the permission path at a 1 kHz tick, which checks state, freshness, and lease. The permission path sends admitted command u t to drive registers and then drives and motors; a red trip line from the permission path sends drive inhibit to the drives and motors. (b) Collapsed, host writes drives: inside a red dashed box labeled one failure domain, the application processor sends an unchecked register write straight to the drive registers, which feed the drives and motors.

figures.title: Illustrative out-of-band interlock and STO path
figures.caption: **Illustrative out-of-band interlock and STO path**: Each emergency-stop contact holds its own force-guided relay, and each relay's enable contact holds one of the drive's two STO inputs, so a single welded contact or shorted wire leaves the other channel able to remove torque. The EDM contacts report a relay that failed to release before restart. Removing torque leaves the motor free to coast; the spring-applied brake is a separate circuit that clamps when its supply is removed. The diagram shows a hardware response path, not a certified integrity level or a stopping distance (synthesized from ISO 13849-1 and IEC 61800-5-2).
figures.alt: Two-channel schematic. A red positive-break E-stop is mechanically linked to two normally closed contacts, S1 and S2, each fed from 24 volts. S1 feeds the coil of force-guided relay K1 and S2 the coil of relay K2; each relay has a normally open enable contact and a normally closed EDM contact. K1 sends STO1 enable and K2 sends STO2 enable to two STO terminals on the drive, which feed the gate-drive supply and then the inverter bridge driving motor M. A red tag above the motor reads tau equals 0, and a note below reads may coast. The two EDM contacts are wired in series with a dashed teal line to a reset monitor, restart only if K1 and K2 released. At the bottom, a brake supply on its own circuit, switched by K1 and K2, contacts not drawn, feeds a spring brake that clamps on power loss and acts on the motor shaft. A note reads hardware only, no processor in this path.

figures.title: Four-stream action tap tuple
figures.caption: **Four-stream action tap tuple**: Four places a command can be logged, from raw policy intent on the application processor through to measured plant response. Which tap a dataset records decides what the model learns to imitate. The four-tap decomposition is this book's construct; the teleoperation rigs it instruments follow @zhao2023learning and @wu2023gello.
figures.alt: Block diagram. On the application processor, a policy or operator box feeds a kinematic mapping box; tap 1, a req, sits between them and tap 2, a cmd, sits after the mapping. A black-channel link with no shared memory crosses the dashed proposal boundary to the discrete safety MCU, which holds the permission path at a 1 kHz tick. Tap 3, a enf, sits after the permission path, which feeds the drives that close the current loops and apply the torque limit. The drives move the plant, joint encoders measure the motion over an interval, and tap 4, a meas, leaves the encoders. All four taps run down to a synchronized telemetry log stamped with hardware timestamps.

figures.title: One lag, three verdicts
figures.caption: **One lag, three verdicts**: Pairing an observation with an action across an uncompensated lag displaces the recorded state by speed times lag. At `{python} SyncDisplacement.t_lag_str` the transit pairing is `{python} SyncDisplacement.dx_transit_str` off, the faster latch approach exceeds the `{python} SyncDisplacement.clearance_str` clearance, and the guarded approach stays inside it. The clearance tolerates at most `{python} SyncDisplacement.lag_max_fast_str` of lag at `{python} SyncDisplacement.v_fast_str` and `{python} SyncDisplacement.lag_max_guarded_str` at `{python} SyncDisplacement.v_guarded_str`; a full-frame rolling-shutter skew alone spans `{python} SyncDisplacement.t_skew_lo_str` to `{python} SyncDisplacement.t_skew_hi_str`.

Three straight parallel lines: transit at 0.50 meters per second on top, the faster latch approach at 0.10 meters per second, and the guarded approach at 0.03 meters per second at the bottom. A red dashed horizontal line marks the 2 millimeter latch clearance. A dotted vertical line at 35 ms marks the uncompensated lag, with a dot on each line. Red squares where the latch lines cross the clearance are labeled at most 20 ms and at most 66.7 ms. A gray band from 15 to 33 ms marks full-frame rolling-shutter skew.

figures.title: Kinematically isomorphic teleoperation loop
figures.caption: **Kinematically isomorphic teleoperation loop**: The operator moves a leader arm whose joints mirror the follower's, and the host copies joint angles across, as in low-cost leader-follower rigs such as GELLO [@wu2023gello]. Because the leader shares the follower's joint structure, the interface needs no inverse kinematics and inherits none of its singularities (configurations where joints align and the arm loses a direction of motion), preserving the operator's direct joint-level coordination. The loop still closes through the operator: human reaction, command transfer, mechanical response, and display delay all enter the recording as phase lag, so the demonstration carries the operator's delay as if it were policy.
figures.alt: Block diagram of a teleoperation loop. An operator box labeled see, decide, move sends an arrow labeled t hum to a small leader arm with joints q1, q2, and q3. The leader feeds a joint copy box stating q follower equals q leader, noted no inverse kinematics, which sends an arrow labeled t cmd to a larger follower arm with the same three joints, reaching toward a latch across a gap labeled t mech. A dashed arrow runs from the follower down to a workspace camera, whose arrow labeled t disp runs left to a display, which feeds back up to the operator.

figures.title: Covariate shift and intervention curation
figures.caption: **Covariate shift and intervention curation**: (a) The learned policy's own actions choose the states it sees next. The worst-case cost bound grows as $\CovariateDriftBound$ for behavioral cloning and as $\mathcal{O}(\DeviationDisadvantage\BehaviorCloningHorizon\AggregatedSurrogateLoss)$ for aggregation on a recoverable task; these are bound orders, not measured drift. (b) One takeover. The `{python} DataLookbackWindow.t_lookback_str` lookback reaches back past the divergence point; states between divergence and takeover are eligible for expert relabeling while the learner's commands there are masked. After takeover, the enforcer's blend and the operator's reorientation are retained for diagnosis but excluded from expert imitation targets, and only the reviewed segment from measured stabilization to recovery becomes an expert demonstration. Based on @ross2011reduction and @spencer2021feedback.
figures.alt: Two panels. Left: a closed loop in which a learned policy sends an action to the plant, a disturbance enters the plant, and the plant state returns to the policy, with the bound orders big-O of S squared epsilon for behavioral cloning and big-O of u S epsilon for aggregation written inside the loop. Right: tracking error against time, flat until t div and rising under the learner to a peak at t takeover. A dashed segment marks the enforcer blend, an oscillating segment marks the operator's reorientation, and from t stabilize the expert's curve falls smoothly to zero at t rec. A bracket marks a 5-second lookback window ending at t takeover and reaching back past t div. Below the axis, a row names the four intervals: drift, blend, re-orient, and stabilized. A states row marks drift as relabel-eligible, blend and re-orient as excluded, and stabilized as expert recovery. A commands row marks drift, blend, and re-orient as masked and stabilized as expert labels.

figures.title: Generative policy architectures and action chunk denoising
figures.caption: **Generative policy architectures and action chunk denoising**: (a) Sampling represents alternative demonstrated routes instead of their direct-regression mean. (b) Iterative refinement produces a candidate action chunk whose clearance and actuator feasibility still require checking. (c) On the machine's schedule, proposals renew every `{python} LatchContactDeadline.t_chunk_str` while setpoints play every `{python} LatchContactDeadline.t_step_str`, and the bars compare the deployed ACT decoder with an illustrative diffusion head that leaves far less of each renewal period to spare. An admitted chunk crosses the black-channel link into the safety MCU's own double buffer and is checked on every permission tick before the drives act. Buffering alone guarantees neither freshness nor freedom from starvation.
figures.alt: Three-panel diagram. Panel (a) contrasts direct regression, whose single mean arrow runs between two dashed demonstrated routes into an obstacle, with conditional diffusion, where a sample arrow from noise lands in one of two mode regions. Panel (b) shows three denoising stages, from a jagged noise trace at step N through a dashed coarse curve to a smooth action chunk at step 0 marked candidate only. Panel (c) is a timing strip over 125 milliseconds with rows for 40 millisecond ACT inference bars, dashed 48 millisecond diffusion bars with 2 milliseconds of slack, a 60 millisecond lease renewed at the next admission, setpoint ticks every 25 milliseconds, and a dense 1 kilohertz permission tick row. Beside it, a block chain runs from the application processor through a black-channel link to a safety MCU with active and filling buffers, then to the drives.

figures.title: Contact force against brake onset
figures.caption: **Contact force against brake onset**: Counterfactual constant-drive ramps rise as $\NormalContactForce = \ContactStiffness \SpeedAtDetection \TimeInstant$ from touch. At the fast approach, the tripwire fires at `{python} LatchContactDeadline.t_trip_fast_str` and braking can begin at `{python} LatchContactDeadline.t_brake_fast_str`, only `{python} LatchContactDeadline.t_left_fast_str` before the ramp reaches the latch limit. At the guarded approach, brake onset is `{python} LatchContactDeadline.t_brake_guarded_str`, leaving `{python} LatchContactDeadline.t_left_guarded_str`. Each onset includes the same `{python} LatchContactDeadline.t_contact_loop_str` response after its own tripwire crossing. Plate stiffness alone gives the shortest deadlines; the lines do not model actual braking trajectories.
figures.alt: Line plot of force against time since touch. Dashed fast and solid guarded constant-drive ramps rise from the origin through a horizontal tripwire toward the latch limit. Separate vertical markers locate fast brake onset at 2.375 milliseconds and guarded brake onset at 3.25 milliseconds. Brackets run from each onset to its ramp's force-limit crossing, with a short 0.125 millisecond fast interval and a longer guarded interval. A red band lies above the force limit.

Recorded replay, bottom left, feeds a demonstration dataset to the policy and scores the action error, with no path from action back to state. figures.title: Standardized robotic evaluation facility

figures.title: Rolling shutter distortion geometry
figures.caption: **Rolling shutter distortion geometry**: A phone camera's rolling shutter photographs a turning aircraft propeller. Because scanlines are exposed and read sequentially from top to bottom rather than simultaneously, blades that move appreciably during the frame's readout are recorded as curved, disconnected arcs; each row samples the blade at a later instant. On a moving robot the same row-by-row sampling shears straight structures and biases the geometry downstream estimators triangulate. (Credit: [Dick Lyon](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Propellor_with_rolling-shutter_artifact.jpg) / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0).
figures.alt: Photograph from an aircraft window of a propeller and engine nacelle in flight, with sky and ground below. The blades appear as bent, curved shapes, some detached from the hub, instead of straight radial blades.

figures.title: Manipulator kinematic frame tree and temporal dynamics
figures.caption: **Manipulator kinematic frame tree and temporal dynamics**: Articulated seven-joint manipulator geometry (a) and the corresponding coordinate transform tree in ROS \\texttt{tf2} (b), in which every frame has exactly one parent. Each tree edge stores a homogeneous transformation matrix; articulated-arm edges depend on joint state, while mounting and localization edges have their own calibration or estimation premises. The target's pose hangs from the base frame, stamped with the epoch $\\AcquisitionEpoch$ of the wrist-camera measurement that produced it, showing the capture-dated base-frame result. The error discussed here arises when application code instead retains the camera-relative measurement and composes it with current wrist kinematics; a wrist rotation $\\FiniteChange\\JointAngle$ over the interval swings the tool center point by $\\ToolPositionError \\approx \\LeverArmLength\\,\\FiniteChange\\JointAngle$ (adapted from @craig2005introduction and @foote2013tf).

figures.title: Transform staleness and lever-arm error at the latch-release slot
figures.caption: **Transform staleness and lever-arm error at the latch-release slot**: Illustrative finger error over one frame period, with zero ingestion delay assumed to isolate this contribution. A deployed calculation must use full capture-to-use age. The camera-to-slot edge ages by duration $\\FiniteChange \\TimeInstant$. Lateral drift at the velocity bound $\\DriftSpeedBound$ moves the finger by $\\TranslationalDriftError = \\DriftSpeedBound\\,\\FiniteChange \\TimeInstant$, while the wrist turning at $\\JointAngularRate$ swings the fingertip, a lever arm $\\LeverArmLength$ beyond it, by $\\LeverArmSweepError \\approx \\LeverArmLength\\,\\JointAngularRate\\,\\FiniteChange \\TimeInstant$. Composing the stale edge with the current wrist pose adds both to the initial error $\\InitialTrackingError$, so the finger error $\\ToolPositionError \\approx \\InitialTrackingError + \\TranslationalDriftError + \\LeverArmLength\\,\\FiniteChange\\JointAngle$ exceeds the slot tolerance $\\PositionalTaskTolerance$.
figures.alt: Transform staleness at the latch-release slot. A dashed ghost arm shows the wrist and finger as dated by the stale edge at t0, with a dashed circle marking the slot tolerance r_tol around the finger. The current arm at t0 + Δt shows the wrist shifted laterally by e_trans = v_drift Δt and the link of length r_arm turned by Δθ_joint = ω Δt, which swings the finger by e_rot ≈ r_arm Δθ_joint. A red vector from the stale finger position to the current finger, labeled e_tool ≈ e_0 + e_trans + r_arm Δθ_joint, ends well outside the r_tol circle.

figures.title: Hierarchical 3D dynamic scene graph architecture
figures.caption: **Hierarchical 3D dynamic scene graph architecture**: Five-layer spatio-temporal memory organization bridging continuous 3D-indexed metric state stores to symbolic foundation reasoning. Drawn for the warehouse, Layer 1 captures triangular metric mesh geometry; Layer 2 extracts 3D objects and dynamic agents such as a walking person; Layer 3 models topological places via Voronoi freespace clearance spheres ($\\TopologicalPlaceNode_i$); Layer 4 structures architectural rooms and portals; and Layer 5 establishes global building mission topology. Vertical inter-layer edges coordinate upward abstraction (compressing metric surfaces into symbolic entities) and downward grounding (translating task tokens into metric coordinates) (adapted from Rosinol et al. [@rosinol20203d; @rosinol2021kimera] and Hughes et al. [@hughes2022hydra]).

From bottom to top: layer 1, a triangle mesh; layer 2, boxes for mug, tote, cage door, and a dashed box for person; layer 3, four places p1 to p4 drawn as dashed circles joined in a chain; layer 4, rooms aisle 12, cross aisle, and dock bay joined in a row; layer 5, buildings warehouse and loading dock. Thin lines connect each node to its parent in the band above, and the mesh to three of the objects. An upward arrow labeled abstraction and a downward arrow labeled grounding run beside the bands.

figures.title: Free-space erosion at the rack end
figures.caption: **Free-space erosion at the rack end**: (a) Top view. The navigation camera's sightline passes the rack end, so the cross aisle behind the rack is unknown from the moment of capture. A person hidden there can advance at $\\HumanWalkingSpeedBound$ = `{python} RackEndBelief.v_h_str`; the dashed disc is the region that person may occupy when the claim lapses, which stops $\\LocalizationBound + \\ProtectiveClearanceMargin$ short of the hull's front. (b) The depth memory still certifies, $\\FreeSpaceDepth - \\LocalizationBound - \\ProtectiveClearanceMargin - \\HumanWalkingSpeedBound \\TimeInstant$. For the hull's current position it falls from the initial clear distance less localization error and protective clearance to zero at `{python} RackEndBelief.t_exp_ahead_str`, and the frame's `{python} RackEndBelief.t_age_str` age at dispatch is spent before memory receives it; abreast of the rack end, the `{python} RackEndBelief.side_clearance_str` side clearance certifies nothing even at capture.

A pink dashed disc centered on the rack end, clipped to the floor, is labeled reach at T_inv, 0.95 m, and a small ring at its center is labeled at dispatch, 83 mm. Dimensions show D_clear 1.10 m ahead and a side gap of 150 mm between hull and rack. Bottom panel b: certified free depth in millimeters against time since the frame, 0 to 700 ms. figures.title: Spatial belief state machine and transition invariants
figures.caption: **Spatial belief state machine and transition invariants**: Each state carries its invariant inside the box and each edge its guard. Occlusion moves a record from VALID to DEGRADED, where the error bound grows under the declared law, and the bound reaching $\\PositionalTaskTolerance$ or a breach of the validity region moves it to EXPIRED. Every edge back to VALID passes the same evidence guard, so freshness alone cannot restore observability and extrapolation cannot renew validity; leaving UNOBSERVABLE also needs the missing constraint restored.

Two rails above return from DEGRADED and EXPIRED to VALID under the guard fresh evidence and innovation gate and model revalidated. A bus from all three states, labeled observability lost from any state, leads to UNOBSERVABLE, labeled rank-deficient state, below VALID, and an arrow labeled constraint restored plus same guard returns from UNOBSERVABLE to VALID.

figures.title: Grounded intent pipeline architecture across the silicon boundary
figures.caption: **Grounded intent pipeline architecture across the silicon boundary**: Physical AI system architecture partitioning high-capacity deliberative reasoning on the Application Processor (AP) from deterministic safety enforcement on the real-time Safety Microcontroller Unit (MCU). The AP processes multimodal streams (RGB-D vision, natural language prompts, proprioception) through the intent model, whose computed `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.t_intent_infer_str` inference sets its `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.f_intent_str` rate. The 3D cost field box stands for an optional producer family of the VoxPoser kind; the running machine's intent model emits a target pose directly. A producer-side ambiguity filter, which passes only a singleton calibrated prediction set ($|\ConformalPredictionSet| = 1$), rejects ambiguous hypotheses before sending a structured intent proposal over the board-level link into the MCU's own memory; the two processors share no memory. The MCU independently verifies evidence epochs, physical actuator ceilings, and braking stopping reserve before arming the lease timer, whose expiry stops the drives without any message from the application processor; the permission path runs at `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.f_permission_str`, and trajectory admission remains a separate check (synthesized from Huang et al. [-@huang2023voxposer], Ahn et al. [-@ahn2022saycan], and Gray [-@gray1989leases]).
figures.alt: Block diagram split by a dashed vertical boundary. On the application processor side, image, instruction, and state boxes feed an intent model box labeled inference 336 ms, runs at 2 Hz, which feeds a 3D cost field box and then an ambiguity diamond. The no branch leads down to a grounding refusal box; the yes branch crosses the boundary on a board link labeled SPI and DMA with CRC, sequence, and expiry, into a dashed mailbox box in MCU SRAM. On the safety MCU side the mailbox feeds a permission path box labeled 1 kHz tick, which feeds joint drives and arms a lease timer above; a red dashed lease-expiry line runs from the timer to the joint drives.

figures.title: Composing value maps for a grasp request
figures.caption: **Composing value maps for a grasp request**: An original schematic of the value-map interface introduced by VoxPoser [@huang2023voxposer], drawn on one horizontal slice of a voxel grid. figures.title: Intent lease lifecycle
figures.caption: **Intent lease lifecycle**: A proposal waits in `Pending` until admission either refuses it, granting no authority, or arms the lease. While the lease is held, only a renewal with a higher sequence number, a newer capture, and a passing permission check moves it to `Renewed` or keeps it there; a stale renewal is rejected without resetting the timer. The held lease ends in one of three ways: the terminal predicates complete the goal, the timer reaches $\IntentLeaseExpiry$, or a contact limit or evidence loss aborts it. Expiry and abort both start the validated fallback, which the MCU selects for the measured state.
figures.alt: State diagram. A Pending box on the left has an arrow labeled admitted into a large rounded container labeled lease held, timer armed, and a dashed arrow down labeled refused, no authority, to an end marker. Inside the container, Active has a self-loop labeled stale renewal rejected and an arrow labeled renewal to Renewed, which has a self-loop labeled renewal with higher sequence, newer capture, check. From the container, an arrow labeled terminal predicates met leads right to goal complete, and two red arrows lead down, one labeled timer reaches t intent exp to Expired and one labeled contact limit or evidence lost to Aborted. Red arrows lead from Expired and Aborted to a validated fallback box.

figures.title: The stopping budget, row by row
figures.caption: **The stopping budget, row by row**: Each bar illustrates the cumulative distance required as each successive physical and timing term is incorporated into the budget, evaluated at the vehicle drive limit under loaded conditions on dry concrete. While kinematic braking, fixed margins, actuator onset, lease execution, and perception age collectively remain within the available clearance, the jerk-limited deceleration profile causes the total to exceed the boundary, and the closed-loop tracking inset exacerbates this overrun. The final bar displays the accounted subtotal at the candidate aisle speed, where the remaining clearance must absorb the dispatch-to-admission interval before providing a net safety reserve.
figures.alt: Stacked bar chart of stopping distance in millimeters. figures.title: Planar laser scanner
figures.caption: **Planar laser scanner**: A rotating mirror sweeps a time-of-flight beam across a horizontal fan, so the device reports range over one plane around the base. A safety-rated scanner of this form adds an early warning field and a protective field. The warning field requests earlier deceleration; the protective field's safety output feeds a controller that selects a risk-assessed stop. Protective-field length must include scanner response, controller and drive delay, braking travel, and uncertainty; a moving base does not become safe merely because motor torque is removed. (Photograph: [Björn Heller](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Sick_laserscanner.jpg) / Wikimedia Commons, [CC BY-SA 3.0 DE](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/de/deed.en).)

figures.title: Illustrative emergency-stop circuit
figures.caption: **Illustrative emergency-stop circuit**: Stages 1 and 2 are the out-of-band interlock circuit (Chapter 4); Stage 3 maps to the numbered list above. Two linked contacts each hold a force-guided relay, the relays' enable contacts hold the drive's two Safe Torque Off (STO) inputs, and their EDM contacts in series block a restart after a weld. The spring-applied brake runs on its own supply, and a supply contactor, if fitted, provides galvanic disconnection. A moving motor can coast after STO, so the brake's set time and the physical stopping distance must be measured for the load and state.
figures.alt: Two-channel schematic in three labeled stages. Stage 1, dual-channel E-stop: a red positive-break E-stop mechanically linked to normally closed contacts S1 and S2, each fed from 24 volts. Stage 2, redundant relays with EDM: S1 drives the coil of force-guided relay K1 and S2 the coil of K2; each relay has a normally open enable contact and a normally closed EDM contact, and the EDM contacts in series run with a dashed teal line to a reset monitor, restart only if K1 and K2 released. Stage 3, separate stop functions: K1 and K2 send STO1 and STO2 enable to the drive, whose gate-drive supply feeds an inverter bridge driving motor M, tagged in red tau equals 0 and noted may coast. A dashed box above the drive reads supply contactor, if fitted. A brake supply on its own circuit, switched by K1 and K2, contacts not drawn, feeds a spring brake that clamps on power loss and acts on the motor shaft, with a dashed tag reading brake set time: measure.

figures.title: Fallback responses and the paths that run them
figures.caption: **Fallback responses and the paths that run them**: The plant state and the failed check select one response directly; the four are alternatives, not steps of an escalation. PROJECT, HOLD, and STOP run in the safety MCU's firmware and reach the drives through its arbiter, which here passes the projected command. INHIBIT is the one response that survives loss of the MCU itself, so it bypasses the arbiter on a hardware path that removes gate-drive supply and lets the spring brakes set. On a moving machine that path also removes motor braking, and the machine coasts until the separately qualified brakes take hold.

figures.title: A cooldown that outlasts the load
figures.caption: **A cooldown that outlasts the load**: Top, the junction relaxes from the `{python} RejectedPlacementThrottle.t_start_str`$\\,^{\circ}\text{C}$ trip threshold toward its `{python} RejectedPlacementThrottle.t_target_str`$\\,^{\circ}\text{C}$ baseline along @eq-placement-cooling-recovery, falling fastest at the moment the load stops and flattening afterward; the clock stays halved until the curve crosses `{python} RejectedPlacementThrottle.t_clear_str`$\\,^{\circ}\text{C}$ at `{python} RejectedPlacementThrottle.t_recov_str`. Bottom: a horizontal time axis from 0 to 1,000 microseconds with two bars, each an execution segment followed by a hatched 90 microsecond block for blocking and interference. figures.title: Authority states and their guards
figures.caption: **Authority states and their guards**: Each box is one value of the per-channel authority state, with its code name above its plain name. A handover runs from request through acknowledgment to a commit on a control tick; from then on the enforcer owns the blend between latched endpoints, and manual proposals begin only when the profile completes with a live manual lease. Timeout, lease lapse, or an invalid state leads to the validated fallback, whose only exit is a reset from rest with a fresh re-admission. The hardwired protective input preempts every state.
figures.alt: State diagram with six boxes. Autonomous, Handover-Pending, Blend, Human-Manual, and Fallback sit inside a dashed enclosure. Arrows run from Autonomous to Handover-Pending on request, from Handover-Pending to Blend on acknowledgment and commit, directly from Autonomous to Blend on an operator acknowledgment, and from Blend to Human-Manual when the profile completes with a valid manual lease. Arrows from Autonomous, Handover-Pending, Blend, and Human-Manual lead to Fallback on lease expiry, timeout, invalid state, or lease lapse. A dashed arrow returns from Fallback to Autonomous on reset from rest. One arrow from the enclosure leads to the Protective state on a hardwired protective input or critical fault.

figures.title: The machine under test and its witnesses
figures.caption: **The machine under test and its witnesses**: Each fault enters at a physical interface of the production machine, F1 at the proposer, F2 on the camera link, F3 on the fieldbus, and F4a and F4b on the supply, and every event the oracle scores is recorded by an instrument on its own clock and supply. F4a steps the supply itself, because the drive transient alone leaves the depleted bus above the converter lockout, and F4b opens the permission rail's feed, whose hold-up must outlast the time from flag to brakes set under the qualified loaded envelope; the figure's duration uses the optimistic all-weight screen (notebook \ref{nbk-verification-supply-headroom}).

The left frame, the machine under test, holds a camera feeding an application SoC running the chunk policy, a board link carrying proposals down to a safety microcontroller running the permission path at 1 kHz, a fieldbus down to the base drives, and torque down to the loaded base on the test floor. On the left, a drive bus at 47.7 V feeds the drives directly and the SoC through a converter with a 33 V lockout; an isolated converter with a 2.0 s held-up rail feeds the microcontroller. Red badges mark injection points F1 at the SoC, F2 on the camera link, F3 on the fieldbus, F4a at the drive bus with a sag to 37.8 V, 4.8 V above lockout and a 150 A step to cross, and F4b at the isolated converter with an illustrative 1,313 ms from flag to brakes set under the optimistic all-weight screen. The right frame, independent witnesses on their own clock and supply, holds a reference clock with trigger line, a logic analyzer, a fieldbus sniffer, current probes, encoders with a high-speed camera, and a rail digitizer, each tapped by a dashed line from the matching point on the machine.

figures.caption: **One F1 trace against its oracle**: Model timelines, not measurements, of the channels an F1 trial must witness at `{python} RackEndVerification.v_aisle_str`, timed from the last valid renewal. The on-time curve travels `{python} RackEndVerification.travel_nominal_str`; the tracking inset is an allowance in the oracle, not extra travel in either curve.
figures.alt: Two stacked panels sharing time after the last valid renewal. The upper panel, from 0 to 130 milliseconds, shows five logic channels, each labeled with its witness instrument: proposer renewals with a pulse at 0, a task-killed mark just after it, and a refused probe at 65 ms; the chunk lease high until it expires at 60 ms; the stop command rising at the next tick, 61 ms; the drive frame rising at 62 ms; and powered deceleration rising at the 82 ms bound in green, with a dashed red trace rising at 112 ms and a 30 ms onset margin marked between them. A shaded onset allowance spans 62 to 82 ms. The lower panel, from 0 to about 1,200 ms, shows base speed falling in an S-curve from 1.3 m/s to rest at 1,013 ms for the green trace, 711.9 mm of nominal travel with 40 mm of distance allowance remaining, and at 1,043 ms for the dashed red trace, 750.9 mm and a positive distance margin of 1 mm against the 751.9 mm oracle.

figures.title: Closed causal loop
figures.caption: **Closed causal loop**: The Brain proposes across the proposal boundary, and the permission path in the Nervous System admits, modifies, or refuses each proposal before the Body acts. The Body's current becomes force and motion at the Boundary, the World evolves, and the Boundary returns measurements with capture times to the permission path and the Brain. Not every state of the World reaches a sensor. The governance envelope surrounds all five levels and changes on the timescale of releases rather than control cycles. The labels are this machine's values: the intent model proposes at `{python} LoopSynthesisFigure.intent_rate_str`, the chunk is renewed every `{python} LoopSynthesisFigure.renewal_str`, the application processor sends a setpoint every `{python} LoopSynthesisFigure.setpoint_str` over a black-channel link to a discrete safety microcontroller unit (MCU) whose permission path ticks at `{python} LoopSynthesisFigure.permission_str`, and the drives close their current loops at `{python} LoopSynthesisFigure.current_loop_str` from a `{python} LoopSynthesisFigure.bus_str` bus. Another machine sets its own rates.
figures.alt: Five stacked levels inside a dashed governance envelope: Brain, Nervous System, Body, Boundary, and World, with a dashed proposal boundary between the Brain and the Nervous System. Inside the Nervous System an application processor sends setpoints over a black-channel link to a discrete safety MCU that runs the permission path. Arrows run from the Brain to the application processor, labeled proposal, from the safety MCU to the Body, labeled admitted command, and on to the World, labeled current in a winding and force and motion. A return arrow runs from the World to the Boundary, then up a side lane to the safety MCU, labeled fresh state, and to the Brain, labeled observations. Labels give the intent model 2 Hz with 336 ms inference, chunk renewal every 50 ms, a setpoint every 25 ms, a 1 kHz permission tick, a 20 kHz current loop in the drives, and a 47.7 V drive bus; the Boundary is event-timed, the World is continuous, and governance has no control rate.

figures.title: Three machine classes in one packaging cell
figures.caption: **Three machine classes in one packaging cell**: (a) The carriage is the moving mass whose impact deforms carton and frame, the insertion head applies the contact force that can buckle a carton wall, and the drive dissipates heat that ages winding insulation. (b) The assumed delay chain from gate closure to full braking totals `{python} PackagingCell.delay_str`. (c) At `{python} PackagingCell.v_nom_str` the carriage travels `{python} PackagingCell.blind_nom_str` before braking begins and stops after `{python} PackagingCell.stop_nom_str`, far beyond the `{python} PackagingCell.clearance_str` stop line; at the restricted `{python} PackagingCell.v_clamp_str` it stops in `{python} PackagingCell.stop_clamp_str`, clear of the `{python} PackagingCell.reserve_str` reserve. All inputs are hypothetical design allocations, not measurements.
figures.alt: Three panels. Panel a is a side-view schematic of a linear track with a drive box at the left end, a carriage carrying a carton, an insertion head pressing down on the carton, and a gate with a red dashed stop line at the right; labels name the drive as thermal dissipation with insulation aging, the carriage as moving mass whose impact deforms carton and frame, and the insertion head as contact force that buckles the carton wall. Panel b is a horizontal delay bar of four segments, image 16 ms, transfer inference and admission 36 ms, bus 2 ms, and brake onset 10 ms, totaling 64 ms from closure. Panel c shows two stopping-distance bars on a millimeter axis from 0 to 180 with a red dashed stop line at 60 mm and a hatched reserve band just before it. At 1.5 m/s the bar has 96 mm of delay travel and 75 mm of braking, reaching 171 mm, with the part beyond the stop line shaded red. At 0.5 m/s the bar has 32 mm of delay travel and a short braking segment, stopping at 40.3 mm with 19.7 mm to spare.

figures.title: Probabilistic octree volumetric mapping
figures.caption: **Probabilistic octree volumetric mapping**: A corridor traversal reconstructed from raw point cloud into a probabilistic octree and then into explicit free, occupied, and unknown space [@hornung2013octomap]. The third panel is what distinguishes spatial memory from an accumulated point cloud, because raycasting records evidence of emptiness along sightlines, letting the map actively retire a phantom obstacle track instead of waiting for a timeout to expire it. (Image: @hornung2013octomap, Autonomous Intelligent Systems Lab, University of Freiburg.)
figures.alt: Probabilistic 3D Volumetric Mapping and Hierarchical Octree Space Subdivision. Empirical 3D spatial memory representation reconstructed from a physical mobile robot traversing an indoor corridor with a tilting lidar scanner. (a) Raw 3D point cloud acquired during robot motion, subject to sensor noise and finite field-of-view occlusions. (b) Volumetric OctoMap voxel representation modeling 3D space as an 8-ary hierarchical tree, where occupied volumes are probabilistically updated and stored across variable resolutions. (c) Explicit free-space raycasting and lossless octree pruning, differentiating observed free cells (white voxels) from occupied obstacles (dark voxels) and unobserved unknown regions; free evidence alone does not certify traversability for a particular robot. By maintaining explicit free-space evidence along sensor sightlines, spatial memory actively invalidates phantom obstacle tracks without waiting for arbitrary software timeouts. (Image: Hornung et al., Autonomous Intelligent Systems Lab, University of Freiburg.)

figures.title: Diffusion policy architecture
figures.caption: **Diffusion policy architecture**: A continuous trajectory diffusion policy for visuomotor control, denoising a candidate action chunk from Gaussian noise across $\DecoderEvaluationCount$ iterations and dispatching only a prefix of it before re-planning. Asynchronous buffering and an independent high-rate permission path can separate slower chunk generation from actuation. Conditional denoising can represent alternative demonstrated paths without taking their direct-regression mean. (Adapted from @chi2024diffusionpolicy).
figures.alt: Three-column block diagram. Observation: camera images and robot state pass through an encoder to a conditioning history. Denoising: Gaussian noise enters a noise network run for a number of sequential steps, producing a dashed candidate action chunk. Dispatch: a bracket marks the prediction horizon; the first segment is sent and the rest discarded. The sent prefix crosses a dashed proposal boundary into a 1 kHz permission path, which passes an admitted command to the drives.

figures.actual_question: Which parts of diffusion policy generation are proposals, and which path admits physical action?
figures.actual_scope: Diffusion iterations are inference evaluations, not physical time steps. A generated or sent prefix is still a proposal until permission admits it.

actual_steps.title: Condition on recent observations
actual_steps.description: Camera images and robot state are encoded into a conditioning history. The history shapes the generated proposal rather than bypassing admission.

actual_steps.title: Generate a multi-step candidate
actual_steps.description: Sequential noise-network evaluations refine a noisy chunk. The resulting horizon contains proposed future action steps, distinct from the denoising computation count.

actual_steps.title: Send only the prefix
actual_steps.description: The execution prefix is sent while the unexecuted tail is discarded before replanning. Committing fewer steps permits later observations to influence a new proposal.

actual_steps.title: Admit commands independently
actual_steps.description: The prefix crosses the proposal boundary into the permission path. Only admitted commands reach the drives and can become physical work.

figures.title: Diffusion policy action chunk denoising and receding-horizon decoupling
figures.caption: **Diffusion policy action chunk denoising and receding-horizon decoupling**: (a) Multimodal resolution: direct regression with mean squared error averages divergent demonstrations into an invalid obstacle collision, whereas conditional diffusion can sample alternative demonstrated modes; generated paths still require clearance checks. (b) Iterative trajectory denoising: starting from Gaussian noise $\ActionChunk^{\DecoderEvaluationCount} \sim \GaussianDistribution(\ZeroVector, \IdentityMatrix)$, reverse diffusion progressively resolves a coarse trajectory into a smooth action chunk $\ActionChunk^0$. (c) Dual-rate decoupling: an asynchronous sampler on the application processor sends each chunk over a black-channel link to a discrete $1\\,\text{kHz}$ safety microcontroller, which holds it in its own double buffer and runs the freshness check, spline interpolation, and slew clamping. The two processors share no memory. (Adapted from @chi2024diffusionpolicy).
figures.alt: Three-panel schematic. Panel a: direct regression averages two demonstrated paths around an obstacle into a mean path that runs into it, while conditional diffusion samples from noise toward one of two mode regions. Panel b: three stacked boxes go from a noisy zigzag to a coarse dashed curve to a smooth candidate action chunk. Panel c: an application processor sampler at 15 Hz sends a chunk through a dashed black-channel link with CRC and sequence number to a safety microcontroller with its own memory, holding an active and a filling buffer and running a freshness check, spline, and slew clamp at a 1 kHz tick; it passes an admitted command to the drives.

figures.actual_question: How do alternative action modes, denoising, and dual-rate dispatch fit together?
figures.actual_scope: The image is a schematic. Candidate paths still require clearance checks; the board link connects processors with distinct memories.

actual_steps.title: Avoid averaging incompatible routes
actual_steps.description: The direct-regression mean passes through the obstacle between two demonstrated modes. Conditional sampling can select an alternative mode, although it does not certify clearance.

actual_steps.title: Refine in inference time
actual_steps.description: The center column goes from noise through a coarse candidate to an action chunk. These refinement stages do not depict the robot physically executing the noisy paths.

actual_steps.title: Transfer across processor boundaries
actual_steps.description: The asynchronous application sampler sends the chunk with CRC and sequence information over the black-channel link. It does not write shared MCU memory.

actual_steps.title: Check before physical dispatch
actual_steps.description: The safety MCU owns active and filling buffers and runs freshness, spline, and slew checks on its fast tick. Only the admitted command proceeds to the drives.

figures.title: The S·P·A intersection landscape
figures.caption: **The S·P·A intersection landscape**: Sense, Plan, and Act meet pairwise in three physical decisions, locating the object now, checking that proposed motion fits limits, and measuring what changed after acting. Their center is the permission decision, where an independent permission path checks the shared physical budget before actuation.

figures.actual_question: Where do sensing, planning, and actuation share a physical decision?
figures.actual_scope: S·P·A is a diagnostic locator, not a replacement architecture or proof of safety. The central permission path is independent of the learned proposer.

actual_steps.title: Locate the object now
actual_steps.description: Sense carries age and location. At Sense ∩ Plan, the handoff must put the object in the current timed and framed state needed for a motion proposal.

actual_steps.title: Check what acting changed
actual_steps.description: Act ∩ Sense asks what changed after force and motion. Feedback needs a new physical observation, not merely a propagated estimate or a task-completion token.

actual_steps.title: Check whether motion fits
actual_steps.description: Plan ∩ Act asks whether the proposed path fits physical limits. A task-level goal does not establish feasible derivatives, clearance, or fallback.

actual_steps.title: Admit only within the shared budget
actual_steps.description: At the center, the independent permission decision checks the relevant shared physical budgets before actuation. The three interfaces locate which contract broke; none alone grants authority.
